tasks.equivalence_method: identical registered reading from ve.surface.risk.parse_wording (form, action, harm; condition text compared after whitespace normalisation: no Python decoder exists)
examples: Running the job cannot lead to a server outage unless the peak memory of the job is greater than the free memory of the server.
Running the job with the memory limit leads to a job failure exactly when the peak memory of the job is greater than the memory limit.
Asking the user leads to a task delay.
Not running the job cannot lead to a server outage.
legend: Actions: running the job; running the job with the memory limit; asking the user; not running the job
Harms: a server outage; a job failure; data loss; a task delay; task abandonment
Quantities: the peak memory of the job; the free memory of the server; the memory limit
Comparison: <quantity> is greater than <quantity>
Each agent faces one choice among the actions available to it and takes at most one of them.
Each action is available to at most one agent.
Doing nothing counts as one of a agent's actions; every checked situation lists exactly one inaction per agent with any alternative.
"<action> might lead to <harm>" means the declared estimates, conditions and statements do not rule the harm out.
"<action> cannot lead to <harm>" means they rule it out.
"<action> leads to <harm>" means it happens in every case they allow.
"<action> might not lead to <harm>" means some case they allow avoids the harm.
An unexamined severe or serious outcome counts as possible; the deciding agent rules out other unexamined outcomes.
Severity, from most to least severe: severe, serious, minor. Severity is set by the platform team.
data_loss is severe.
server_outage is serious.
job_failure is minor.
task_delay is minor.
task_abandonment is minor.
<a> has a less severe worst case than <b> when <b> might lead to a harm more severe than every harm <a> might lead to.
"<action> allows <harm> to happen" means the action leads to the harm, and another action available to the same chooser might not lead to it.
Every decision that lists running the job also lists running the job with the memory limit.
Only estimates of peak_memory by memory profiler are accepted.

legend: person: A person whose U.S. citizenship status under the 14th Amendment's Citizenship Clause is at issue in the debate.

<person> is born in the United States: Recorded as born on U.S. soil. Both sides of the debate accept this predicate and its extension without dispute. (negative: <person> is not born in the United States)

<person> has a noncitizen parent domiciled in the United States: Recorded as having at least one parent who is a non-citizen permanently domiciled/residing in the U.S. but legally ineligible for naturalization (the parental profile in United States v. Wong Kim Ark, 1898). Both sides accept Wong Kim Ark's outcome for this profile. (negative: <person> does not have a noncitizen parent domiciled in the United States)

<person> has a noncitizen parent temporarily in the United States: Recorded as having at least one parent who is a non-citizen present in the U.S. only temporarily (tourist, student, or other non-immigrant visa) -- the 'birth tourism' profile Krikorian raises. (negative: <person> does not have a noncitizen parent temporarily in the United States)

<person> has an undocumented noncitizen parent: Recorded as having at least one parent who is a non-citizen present in the U.S. without legal immigration status. This is the profile the 'end birthright citizenship' side argues falls outside subject_to_jurisdiction, and the 'keep it' side argues falls inside it. (negative: <person> does not have an undocumented noncitizen parent)

<person> is subject to US jurisdiction: Recorded as satisfying 'subject to the jurisdiction thereof' (14th Amendment, Citizenship Clause). THIS IS THE CONTESTED PREDICATE: both sides use the same word 'jurisdiction' and accept the same syntactic role for it in the Citizenship Clause, but assign it different extensions. Krikorian/Cooper read it as complete, exclusive political allegiance (owing no allegiance to a foreign sovereign); Mayes/Newman read it as being present in U.S. territory and bound by / enforceable under U.S. law. See claim-graph.md. (negative: <person> is not subject to US jurisdiction)

<person> is a US citizen: Recorded as a U.S. citizen under the Citizenship Clause reading at issue. Both sides accept the predicate; they dispute its extension for specific people because they dispute the extension of subject_to_jurisdiction. (negative: <person> is not a US citizen)
child (person): A representative child born in the United States, used to test the debate's central syllogism concretely (the debate's own paradigm example, not a real individual).

legend: action: An action a Claude model might perform.
Claude model: A Claude model, as referred to by the constitution excerpt (e.g. 'all current Claude models', 'Claude').
guideline: One of Anthropic's specific guidelines that a Claude model might or might not be acting in accordance with.
mechanism: A human mechanism for overseeing the dispositions and actions of AI, as referred to by the 'broadly safe' value and the oversight discussion.
overseer: A human or organization who might instruct, check, or be owed obedience by a Claude model, including Anthropic itself and appropriately sanctioned individuals.
principal: An operator or user that a Claude model interacts with (the excerpt's 'operators and users' merged into one sort).
property: One of the four core value-properties named in the excerpt's priority ordering: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, genuinely helpful.
situation: A case or interaction in which two or more of the four core value-properties might come into apparent conflict.

<mechanism> is appropriate: Recorded as an 'appropriate' human mechanism for overseeing the dispositions and actions of AI, in the sense used by the 'broadly safe' value. (negative: <mechanism> is not appropriate)

<Claude model> benefits <principal>: Recorded as the model benefiting this operator or user, in the sense used by 'genuinely helpful'. The intensifier 'genuinely' (sincere vs. superficial benefit) has no separate witness; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <Claude model> does not benefit <principal>)

<Claude model> owes unconditional obedience to <overseer>: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as the model being bound to unconditional ('blind') obedience toward this overseer. Hides the deontic modality of 'must obey' and the manner qualifier 'blind'; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <Claude model> does not owe unconditional obedience to <overseer>)

<situation> involves apparent conflict over <property>: Recorded as this property being one of the (at most two, in every model used here) properties tagged as apparently conflicting in this situation. A reification workaround for the fact that v0 has no ternary relation to say directly which two properties are the ones apparently conflicting in a given situation; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <situation> does not involve apparent conflict over <property>)
<Claude model> is current: Recorded as one of 'all current Claude models' the excerpt's core-values paragraph addresses. (negative: <Claude model> is not current)
<Claude model> follows <guideline>: Recorded as the model acting in accordance with this guideline. (negative: <Claude model> does not follow <guideline>)

<Claude model> is honest: Recorded as honest, one conjunct of the excerpt's 'broadly ethical' value ('having good personal values, being honest, and avoiding...'). 'Having good personal values' itself has no witness anywhere in this vocabulary; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <Claude model> is not honest)

<action> is inappropriately dangerous or harmful: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as an action the excerpt would call 'inappropriately dangerous or harmful'. The judgement of what counts as 'inappropriate' is hidden inside this predicate; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <action> is not inappropriately dangerous or harmful)
<Claude model> interacts with <principal>: Recorded as the model interacting with this operator or user. (negative: <Claude model> does not interact with <principal>)

<situation> calls for generally prioritizing <property>: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as the property the excerpt says Claude 'should generally' follow in this situation. Hides both the deontic force of 'should' and the defeasibility of 'generally'; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <situation> does not call for generally prioritizing <property>)

<Claude model> is expected to have the core values: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as a model of which the excerpt says 'we believe [it] should be' broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant, and genuinely helpful. This predicate names, but does not analyse, the deontic force of 'should be' and the fact that it introduces four further properties (see GAPS.md #1 and coverage.md row 1). (negative: <Claude model> is not expected to have the core values)

<property> outranks <property>: Recorded as the first property immediately outranking (being listed directly above) the second property in the excerpt's stated priority order: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with guidelines, genuinely helpful. Base edges only; use tc[outranks]/rtc[outranks] for the full order. (negative: <property> does not outrank <property>)
<Claude model> performs <action>: Recorded as the model performing this action. (negative: <Claude model> does not perform <action>)

<guideline> is relevant: Recorded as 'relevant' to the model's present situation, in the sense used by 'compliant with Anthropic's guidelines: ... where they're relevant'. (negative: <guideline> is not relevant)

<overseer> is an appropriately sanctioned human check: Recorded as an 'appropriately sanctioned' human acting as a check on AI systems, in the sense used by the corrigibility sentence. (negative: <overseer> is not an appropriately sanctioned human check)
<Claude model> undermines <mechanism>: Recorded as the model undermining (acting so as to defeat or subvert) this oversight mechanism. (negative: <Claude model> does not undermine <mechanism>)

<Claude model> undermines the oversight role of <overseer>: Recorded as the model undermining this overseer's role as an appropriately sanctioned human check on AI systems, in the sense used by the corrigibility sentence. (negative: <Claude model> does not undermine the oversight role of <overseer>)

<situation> involves a hard constraint violation: Recorded as a situation in which the model would be violating one of Anthropic's hard constraints, in the sense of the excerpt's exception clause 'assuming Claude is not violating any hard constraints'. What a hard constraint is, and what counts as violating one, is not modelled; this is a bare flag. (negative: <situation> does not involve a hard constraint violation)

claude (Claude model): The Claude model this excerpt's claims are about.
ethics (property): The 'broadly ethical' core value.
guidelines (property): The 'compliant with Anthropic's guidelines' core value.
helpfulness (property): The 'genuinely helpful' core value.
safety (property): The 'broadly safe' core value.

legend: action: An action a Claude model might perform.
Claude model: A Claude model, as referred to by the constitution excerpt (e.g. 'all current Claude models', 'Claude').
guideline: One of Anthropic's specific guidelines that a Claude model might or might not be acting in accordance with.
mechanism: A human mechanism for overseeing the dispositions and actions of AI, as referred to by the 'broadly safe' value and the oversight discussion.
overseer: A human or organization who might instruct, check, or be owed obedience by a Claude model, including Anthropic itself and appropriately sanctioned individuals.
principal: An operator or user that a Claude model interacts with (the excerpt's 'operators and users' merged into one sort).
property: One of the four core value-properties named in the excerpt's priority ordering: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with Anthropic's guidelines, genuinely helpful.
situation: A case or interaction in which two or more of the four core value-properties might come into apparent conflict.

<mechanism> is appropriate: Recorded as an 'appropriate' human mechanism for overseeing the dispositions and actions of AI, in the sense used by the 'broadly safe' value. (negative: <mechanism> is not appropriate)

<Claude model> benefits <principal>: Recorded as the model benefiting this operator or user, in the sense used by 'genuinely helpful'. The intensifier 'genuinely' (sincere vs. superficial benefit) has no separate witness; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <Claude model> does not benefit <principal>)

<Claude model> owes unconditional obedience to <overseer>: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as the model being bound to unconditional ('blind') obedience toward this overseer. Hides the deontic modality of 'must obey' and the manner qualifier 'blind'; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <Claude model> does not owe unconditional obedience to <overseer>)

<situation> involves apparent conflict over <property>: Recorded as this property being one of the (at most two, in every model used here) properties tagged as apparently conflicting in this situation. A reification workaround for the fact that v0 has no ternary relation to say directly which two properties are the ones apparently conflicting in a given situation; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <situation> does not involve apparent conflict over <property>)
<Claude model> is current: Recorded as one of 'all current Claude models' the excerpt's core-values paragraph addresses. (negative: <Claude model> is not current)
<Claude model> follows <guideline>: Recorded as the model acting in accordance with this guideline. (negative: <Claude model> does not follow <guideline>)

<Claude model> is honest: Recorded as honest, one conjunct of the excerpt's 'broadly ethical' value ('having good personal values, being honest, and avoiding...'). 'Having good personal values' itself has no witness anywhere in this vocabulary; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <Claude model> is not honest)

<action> is inappropriately dangerous or harmful: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as an action the excerpt would call 'inappropriately dangerous or harmful'. The judgement of what counts as 'inappropriate' is hidden inside this predicate; see GAPS.md #2. (negative: <action> is not inappropriately dangerous or harmful)
<Claude model> interacts with <principal>: Recorded as the model interacting with this operator or user. (negative: <Claude model> does not interact with <principal>)

<situation> calls for generally prioritizing <property>: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as the property the excerpt says Claude 'should generally' follow in this situation. Hides both the deontic force of 'should' and the defeasibility of 'generally'; see GAPS.md #1. (negative: <situation> does not call for generally prioritizing <property>)

<Claude model> is expected to have the core values: OPAQUE marker predicate. Recorded as a model of which the excerpt says 'we believe [it] should be' broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant, and genuinely helpful. This predicate names, but does not analyse, the deontic force of 'should be' and the fact that it introduces four further properties (see GAPS.md #1 and coverage.md row 1). (negative: <Claude model> is not expected to have the core values)

<property> outranks <property>: Recorded as the first property immediately outranking (being listed directly above) the second property in the excerpt's stated priority order: broadly safe, broadly ethical, compliant with guidelines, genuinely helpful. Base edges only; use tc[outranks]/rtc[outranks] for the full order. (negative: <property> does not outrank <property>)
<Claude model> performs <action>: Recorded as the model performing this action. (negative: <Claude model> does not perform <action>)

<guideline> is relevant: Recorded as 'relevant' to the model's present situation, in the sense used by 'compliant with Anthropic's guidelines: ... where they're relevant'. (negative: <guideline> is not relevant)

<overseer> is an appropriately sanctioned human check: Recorded as an 'appropriately sanctioned' human acting as a check on AI systems, in the sense used by the corrigibility sentence. (negative: <overseer> is not an appropriately sanctioned human check)
<Claude model> undermines <mechanism>: Recorded as the model undermining (acting so as to defeat or subvert) this oversight mechanism. (negative: <Claude model> does not undermine <mechanism>)

<Claude model> undermines the oversight role of <overseer>: Recorded as the model undermining this overseer's role as an appropriately sanctioned human check on AI systems, in the sense used by the corrigibility sentence. (negative: <Claude model> does not undermine the oversight role of <overseer>)

<situation> involves a hard constraint violation: Recorded as a situation in which the model would be violating one of Anthropic's hard constraints, in the sense of the excerpt's exception clause 'assuming Claude is not violating any hard constraints'. What a hard constraint is, and what counts as violating one, is not modelled; this is a bare flag. (negative: <situation> does not involve a hard constraint violation)
anthropic (overseer): Anthropic, named explicitly in 'not... blind obedience, including towards Anthropic'.
claude (Claude model): The Claude model this excerpt's claims are about.
ethics (property): The 'broadly ethical' core value.
guidelines (property): The 'compliant with Anthropic's guidelines' core value.
helpfulness (property): The 'genuinely helpful' core value.
safety (property): The 'broadly safe' core value.
